title: Patch topology and w-local affine schemes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ an affine scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $f\in A$, put $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\in X:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and $V(f)=X\setminus D(f)$. The *patch topology* on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] is generated by the subsets $D(f)$ and $V(f)$ for $f\in A$. A subset is *constructible* here [def-weil-constructible-subset] if it is a finite Boolean combination of these subsets. We call $X$ *w-local* if its closed points [def-weil-closed-points] form a closed subset and every connected component has exactly one closed point. In this last sentence, closedness and connected components refer to the Zariski topology; a connected component is a maximal connected subset.

lean.note: For a commutative ring A, use IsWLocalRing A on the underlying space PrimeSpectrum A of Spec A. WLocalSpace gives closed closed-points and unique closed specializations; WLocalSpace.isHomeomorph_connectedComponents_closedPoints identifies this with exactly one closed point per connected component. The converse follows because closed specializations lie in the same connected component. Patch topology, constructible sets, D(f), and V(f) use the listed existing Mathlib declarations; no duplicate definitions.
